examples.state: While Robert Hooke's discovery of cells in 1665 led to the proposal of the Cell Theory, Hooke misled the cell membrane theory that all cells contained a hard cell wall since only plant cells could be observed at the time. Microscopists focused on the cell wall for well over 150 years until advances in microscopy were made. In the early 19th century, cells were recognized as being separate entities, unconnected, and bound by individual cell walls after it was found that plant cells could be separated. This theory extended to include animal cells to suggest a universal mechanism for cell protection and development. By the second half of the 19th century, microscopy was still not advanced enough to make a distinction between cell membranes and cell walls. However, some microscopists correctly identified at this time that while invisible, it could be inferred that cell membranes existed in animal cells due to intracellular movement of components internally but not externally and that membranes weren't the equivalent of a cell wall to plant cell. It was also inferred that cell membranes weren't vital components to all cells. Many refuted the existence of a cell membrane still towards the end of the 19th century. In 1890, an update to the Cell Theory stated that cell membranes existed, but were merely secondary structures. It wasn't until later studies with osmosis and permeability that cell membranes gained more recognition. In 1895, Ernest Overton proposed that cell membranes were made of lipids.
examples.question: does the animal cell have a cell membrane

examples.question: Using only entries observed after the most recent auto_shutdown, how strong is the evidence that device_alpha currently has a thermal regulation problem?

options.name: No relevant observation
options.criteria: No log entries fall after the last auto_shutdown, so there is no time-valid evidence about the current state.

options.name: Observation contradicts the issue
options.criteria: Post-shutdown entries all show temperatures well below threshold with no fault indication, so the evidence indicates the thermal problem is not present.

options.name: Weak and ambiguous
options.criteria: A single post-shutdown entry is borderline or mildly elevated, but time and threshold context leave the current risk uncertain.

options.name: Moderately elevated
options.criteria: Post-shutdown entries show repeated near-threshold readings, suggesting a developing but not yet confirmed thermal problem.

options.name: Strong and repeated
options.criteria: Multiple post-shutdown entries exceed the threshold or show repeated failures, giving strong time-valid evidence of an ongoing thermal regulation problem.
